pathway.title: CNX Resources Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The first finding is leverage and coverage. At September 30, 2026 CNX Resources Corp carried USD 2,278.924 million of balance-sheet debt and USD 1.977 million of cash, which is 1.79x gross and 1.78x net of trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million, against 1.94x at FY2025; trailing cash interest cover is 8.07x. These are management-measure results, not covenant ratios, and a principal-based gross figure is 1.80x (Documentary Fact from the financial handoff; the ratios are calculated there). The mechanic is that adjusted EBITDAX removes unrealized derivative gains but keeps realized settlements, so it tracks cash earnings better than reported revenue, which includes a derivative gain of USD 160.563 million in Q3 2026; the implication is low leverage tolerance risk today, with a cushion that depends on gas prices.

The second finding is liquidity and refinancing. Cash is minimal, so liquidity is revolver capacity: USD 1,140.053 million is unused on the parent revolver (after USD 27.097 million of letters of credit) and USD 533.000 million on the CNXM revolver, which the parent does not guarantee. Undrawn capacity fell from USD 1,790.703 million at March 31, 2026 to USD 1,673.053 million. Both revolvers mature on May 17, 2029, together with USD 299.85 million drawn, so the refinancing risk is concentrated in one year; the notes follow in 2030 (USD 400 million, CNXM), 2031 (USD 500 million), 2032 (USD 600 million) and 2034 (USD 500 million), and nothing falls due in 2026 to 2028 (Documentary Fact).

The third finding is capital allocation. In the nine months of 2026 CNX repurchased shares for USD 432.781 million, while cash purchases of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million by USD 75.178 million, with net revolver borrowings of USD 67.100 million (Analyst Interpretation of cited figures). The convertible notes were settled in shares without cash and the 5.875% notes due 2034 were issued in the same period in which the 6.00% notes due 2029 were repurchased. The mechanic is that discretionary buybacks consume the cash flow that services the revolvers; the program is discretionary and can be reduced, which limits the credit risk if management responds in a price downturn. The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is not stated (Insufficient Information).

The fourth finding is the business risk. Production is 92% natural gas, sold at market prices under short-term contracts in one basin, mainly through Shale; three marketers each exceeded 10% of FY2025 customer revenue. Hedges cover 461.2 Bcf for 2026, 409.4 Bcf for 2027, 233.1 Bcf for 2028 and 38.2 Bcf for 2029, so revenue visibility is about two years. Fixed commitments sit outside the debt figure: unconditional purchase obligations of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds, leases and letters of credit (Documentary Fact). In a weak-price year these fixed costs compress margin against variable revenue.

The fifth finding is structure and information. The parent and CNXM are separate creditor pools: the parent does not guarantee the CNXM notes or revolver and parent covenants exclude CNXM, so consolidated ratios blur which group bears which claim. Covenant compliance is stated for both groups but no ratio or headroom is supplied, and the indentures, credit agreements, ratings and proxy statement are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions, liens and asset transfers is untested (Insufficient Information).

runs.text: Strengths. Low leverage on management's measure and strong interest cover give debt service a wide margin today [Documentary Fact]. There are no maturities before 2029 and the notes are staggered across 2030 to 2034 [Documentary Fact]. A large hedge book, with 461.2 Bcf covered for 2026 and 409.4 Bcf for 2027, supports cash flow visibility for roughly two years [Documentary Fact]. Revolver capacity of USD 1,673.053 million gives liquidity without cash on hand [Documentary Fact]. The business is large and long-lived, with 9.7 Tcfe of proved reserves, 72.2% proved developed, and owned gathering systems that reduce reliance on third parties [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks and the absence of dividends are discretionary, so management can redirect cash to creditors in stress [Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Earnings rest on a management non-GAAP measure and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be shown [Insufficient Information]. Revenue is single-basin, market-priced and short-term, so unhedged volumes and basis follow Appalachian prices, and hedges thin after 2027 [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks exceeded free cash generation in the nine months and revolver borrowings rose [Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity depends on two revolvers that mature together in 2029, one of them at the CNXM level that the parent does not guarantee [Documentary Fact]. Fixed commitments of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds and leases add claims outside the debt figure [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration in a few marketers is a counterparty risk [Documentary Fact]. Governance and legal capacity cannot be tested without the executed documents and the proxy statement [Insufficient Information].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or merger was announced in the pack for the cutoff window. The new debt and related capital actions of the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are as follows. CNX issued 500,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.875% Senior Notes due March 2034 at par under an indenture dated February 26, 2026 with UMB Bank, N.A. as trustee, guaranteed by the restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the CNX Credit Facility; interest is payable on March 1 and September 1 beginning September 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:22). In the same period CNX repurchased all 500,000 of its 6.00% Senior Notes due January 2029, recording a 12,009 loss on debt extinguishment (page:22), and the supplement places that loss in Q1 2026 (Q1 supplement page:12). The 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes matured on May 1, 2026; the remaining 208,553 principal was settled through the issuance of 12,636,743 net shares and no cash was exchanged, and the related capped calls expired with 3,605,684 shares delivered to CNX and retired (page:23). The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is Insufficient Information: the filings state both events but do not link them, so the link is an analyst reading only. The liquidity effect is visible in the balance sheet: the 2026 convertible notes and the January 2029 notes are gone, leaving the May 2029 revolvers as the nearest maturity (accepted financial handoff). The revolver borrowing base and elected commitments were unchanged at 2,400,000 and 1,400,000 on May 13, 2026 (page:19). Earlier, in the nine months ended September 30, 2025, CNX issued 200,000 of additional 7.25% Senior Notes due March 2032 at 100.5% of par (page:23) and on January 27, 2025 acquired Apex Energy II, LLC's upstream and associated midstream business for cash consideration of about 517,599 (page:17). Other 2026 capital actions: share repurchases of 432,781 in the nine months at an average price of 35.08 per share (page:35), and a July 1, 2026 sale of federal tax credits for about 30,000 net of costs, which approximated carrying value (page:18). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 and inside the pack: share count and hedge positions as of October 2026, and updated 2026 guidance in the Q3 supplement (adjusted EBITDAX 1,290 to 1,310 and capital expenditures 571 to 586, US$m, page:7). Draft or pending transactions: none in the pack.

fields.value: CNX Resources Corp is a publicly listed, non-sponsored producer whose business is selling Appalachian natural gas, mostly from Shale and a smaller Coalbed Methane position, through short-term market-priced contracts to a few large marketers, cushioned by a hedge book and supported by owned gathering systems. For a creditor the operating model is stable in volume but exposed to price, basis and counterparty concentration, and its reported revenue includes derivative gains that are largely non-cash. The 2026 transactions are mainly liability management and shareholder returns: new 2034 notes against the repurchase of the 2029 notes, a convertible that matured into shares rather than cash, and buybacks that exceeded free cash generation in the nine months. The pack shows no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no documented priming, uptier or drop-down; that absence is limited to seven filings and is not a clearance, because indentures, credit agreements and the proxy statement are not supplied. The midstream subsidiary sits in a separate credit group with its own notes and revolver, a structural feature rather than an observed behaviour.

It covers the consolidated group (CNX Resources Corporation and subsidiaries), with the parent and the CNX Midstream Partners LP (CNXM) credit groups kept apart, for FY2025 and the periods to Q3 2026. It works from the upstream readiness, financial and business handoffs only and reads no source text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CNX Resources Corp has a moderate credit risk profile on the evidence supplied: low leverage and no maturities before 2029 are offset by single-basin gas price exposure and shareholder returns that ran ahead of free cash flow. The strongest support is debt of USD 2,278.924 million against trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million (1.79x), cash interest cover of 8.07x, USD 1,673.053 million of undrawn facilities and 461.2 Bcf hedged for 2026. The weakest point is that the earnings measure is management's non-GAAP figure, covenant headroom is unverified and nine-month buybacks of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million. Gas prices after the hedges thin in 2028 and 2029, and the pace of buybacks, decide the outcome. [Assessment: Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first finding is leverage and coverage. At September 30, 2026 CNX Resources Corp carried USD 2,278.924 million of balance-sheet debt and USD 1.977 million of cash, which is 1.79x gross and 1.78x net of trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million, against 1.94x at FY2025; trailing cash interest cover is 8.07x. These are management-measure results, not covenant ratios, and a principal-based gross figure is 1.80x (Documentary Fact from the financial handoff; the ratios are calculated there). The mechanic is that adjusted EBITDAX removes unrealized derivative gains but keeps realized settlements, so it tracks cash earnings better than reported revenue, which includes a derivative gain of USD 160.563 million in Q3 2026; the implication is low leverage tolerance risk today, with a cushion that depends on gas prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is liquidity and refinancing. Cash is minimal, so liquidity is revolver capacity: USD 1,140.053 million is unused on the parent revolver (after USD 27.097 million of letters of credit) and USD 533.000 million on the CNXM revolver, which the parent does not guarantee. Undrawn capacity fell from USD 1,790.703 million at March 31, 2026 to USD 1,673.053 million. Both revolvers mature on May 17, 2029, together with USD 299.85 million drawn, so the refinancing risk is concentrated in one year; the notes follow in 2030 (USD 400 million, CNXM), 2031 (USD 500 million), 2032 (USD 600 million) and 2034 (USD 500 million), and nothing falls due in 2026 to 2028 (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third finding is capital allocation. In the nine months of 2026 CNX repurchased shares for USD 432.781 million, while cash purchases of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million by USD 75.178 million, with net revolver borrowings of USD 67.100 million (Analyst Interpretation of cited figures). The convertible notes were settled in shares without cash and the 5.875% notes due 2034 were issued in the same period in which the 6.00% notes due 2029 were repurchased. The mechanic is that discretionary buybacks consume the cash flow that services the revolvers; the program is discretionary and can be reduced, which limits the credit risk if management responds in a price downturn. The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is not stated (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth finding is the business risk. Production is 92% natural gas, sold at market prices under short-term contracts in one basin, mainly through Shale; three marketers each exceeded 10% of FY2025 customer revenue. Hedges cover 461.2 Bcf for 2026, 409.4 Bcf for 2027, 233.1 Bcf for 2028 and 38.2 Bcf for 2029, so revenue visibility is about two years. Fixed commitments sit outside the debt figure: unconditional purchase obligations of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds, leases and letters of credit (Documentary Fact). In a weak-price year these fixed costs compress margin against variable revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth finding is structure and information. The parent and CNXM are separate creditor pools: the parent does not guarantee the CNXM notes or revolver and parent covenants exclude CNXM, so consolidated ratios blur which group bears which claim. Covenant compliance is stated for both groups but no ratio or headroom is supplied, and the indentures, credit agreements, ratings and proxy statement are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions, liens and asset transfers is untested (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Low leverage on management's measure and strong interest cover give debt service a wide margin today [Documentary Fact]. There are no maturities before 2029 and the notes are staggered across 2030 to 2034 [Documentary Fact]. A large hedge book, with 461.2 Bcf covered for 2026 and 409.4 Bcf for 2027, supports cash flow visibility for roughly two years [Documentary Fact]. Revolver capacity of USD 1,673.053 million gives liquidity without cash on hand [Documentary Fact]. The business is large and long-lived, with 9.7 Tcfe of proved reserves, 72.2% proved developed, and owned gathering systems that reduce reliance on third parties [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks and the absence of dividends are discretionary, so management can redirect cash to creditors in stress [Analyst Interpretation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings rest on a management non-GAAP measure and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be shown [Insufficient Information]. Revenue is single-basin, market-priced and short-term, so unhedged volumes and basis follow Appalachian prices, and hedges thin after 2027 [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks exceeded free cash generation in the nine months and revolver borrowings rose [Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity depends on two revolvers that mature together in 2029, one of them at the CNXM level that the parent does not guarantee [Documentary Fact]. Fixed commitments of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds and leases add claims outside the debt figure [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration in a few marketers is a counterparty risk [Documentary Fact]. Governance and legal capacity cannot be tested without the executed documents and the proxy statement [Insufficient Information].
